args.summary: The latest deploy of checkout-api, v2.3.1, began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Mitigation: rolled back all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback completed and verified: v2.3.0 is healthy in all regions with error rate reduced to ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1 must not be redeployed until root cause is identified; it was never healthy in production.
args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed**: checkout-api was running v2.3.1, which was failing health checks with an 18% error rate across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west).
2. **Rolled back** to **v2.3.0** — the most recent release that was healthy in production — in all regions. Verified post-rollback: v2.3.0 is healthy everywhere, error rate down to 0.2%.
3. **Opened incident INC-0001 (SEV2)**, which paged the on-call engineer, documenting the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, and current healthy status.

Recommendation: hold v2.3.1 for root-cause investigation before any redeploy.

Rollback doesn't require approval (it was healthy before). I could do both in parallel, but incident should describe what I did — better to rollback first, then open incident with confirmation. The instruction says make independent calls in same block. The incident content depends on rollback result ("describing what you did"), so I'll do rollback first.

transcript.reasoning_content: Healthy. Now open SEV2 incident describing what was done.
